instructions.question: Does this Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express warm approval or hope, an explicit hostile or distressed feeling, or neither (information, requests, suggestions, banter)?
instructions.rule: Neutral is the default. Data requests, 'why' questions, demands for measures, proposals to fine people, comparisons, serious scolding of careless citizens, sarcasm about testing and city 'league' banter stay neutral, even when critical. Choose negative only for an explicit marker: blame of the authorities or a gathering, a claim the numbers are fake, an insult or curse, a fed-up statement, or the commenter's own fear or despair. Positive needs praise or defence of doctors, the institute or the government, thanks, relief, sincere hope for zero cases, or a short approving word even next to a name tag.

neutral.what: Bare tags, statistics, observations, requests for details, questions, proposals, scolding without insults, comparisons, jokes and banter, including critical or sarcastic ones.
examples: Mbyllni kufinjt mos luani me jetet e njerzve (Close the borders, don't play with people's lives)
Nëse nuk bëjmë asnjë test, s'do të kemi asnjë rast. U zgjidh problemi. (If we do no tests, we'll have no cases. Problem solved.)
Po shihet qe njerezit nuk jane te diciplinuar (It's clear people aren't disciplined)
213 ja pafshim hajrin (May we see good from these 213)
neutral.cues: personal names alone, publikoni (publish), testoni (test), mbyllni (close), pse (why), rrini n'shpi (stay home), ma gjall (livelier), on top, hahaha
neutral.not_for: Blame, fake-number claims, insults or curses, being fed up, or own fear are negative.

positive.what: Praise, thanks or defence of doctors, the institute or the government; congratulations; sincere hope for no cases; cheering at recoveries; short approving words.
examples: Respekt per punen tuaj (Respect for your work)
Në asnjë rast nuk mundemi ta fajsojm qeverin por secili duhet fajsu vehten (In no way can we blame the government, everyone should blame themselves)
shpresoj qe ta kalojmë këtë gjendje me sa më pak pasoja. (I hope we get through this with as few consequences as possible.)
Ali Kastrati mire (Ali Kastrati, good)
positive.cues: bravo (well done), respekt (respect), faleminderit (thanks), urime (congratulations), shpresoj (I hope), inshallah (God willing), asnje rast (no cases), super, nice, mire (good), perher (always), vazhdojm (let's keep going), rrnoft (long live)
positive.not_for: Ironic 'hajr' or 'ma gjall' over new cases, city-ranking banter and bare good-news headlines are neutral.

negative.what: Blame, claims the numbers are invented, insults or curses, fed-up frustration, fear or despair, bitter irony about Kosovo failing.
examples: Qeveria koti ika fajet (The Kurti government is to blame)
Veq shifren e par pja ndrroni se tekstin tjeter veq copy paste po get (You only change the first number, the rest is copy paste)
U ba bajat me ka 200 mo  ndrrone pak (It's stale with 200 a day, change it a bit)
Krejt Rrena (All lies)
negative.cues: faj (blame), rrena/prralla (lies/fairy tales), aparati (the machine), bajat (stale), lodhet (tired), magari (donkey), pisa (dirty one), injorantat (the ignorant), ju raft (may it strike you), Kotit (Kurti's, mocking), tmerr (horror), deshtim (failure)
negative.not_for: Requests, proposals, serious scolding, questions or banter without such a marker are neutral.
